2  	title: Optimizing prefetching
3  	description: Resolve per-link URL data with the prefetch prop, include session data in the App Shell, or exclude expensive content from a prefetch.

18 	---
19 	
20 	Prefetching downloads a route's JavaScript, CSS, and RSC payload before the user navigates to it, so the router can render the next route without waiting for a round trip. The [Prefetching guide](/docs/app/guides/prefetching) covers what the App Router prefetches by default.
21 	
22 	With [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), a [`<Link>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link) prefetches one reusable [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route by default. The App Shell includes the route's static output. For routes that read [`cookies()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/cookies) or [`headers()`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/headers), it also includes session-specific UI. Links to the same route reuse that App Shell.
23 	
24 	The shared App Shell does not include URL data that varies by destination, such as [`searchParams`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#searchparams-optional) and [`params`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/page#params-optional). Set `prefetch={true}` on a link to resolve cached content that depends on its [URL data](/docs/app/glossary#url-data) before navigation instead of streaming that content after navigation.
25 	
26 	This guide assumes [Cache Components](/docs/app/getting-started/caching) with [`partialPrefetching`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching) enabled:
27 	
28 	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={4,5}
29 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
30 	
31 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
32 	  cacheComponents: true,
33 	  partialPrefetching: true,
34 	}
35 	
36 	export default nextConfig
37 	```
38 	
39 	It also assumes your route is already structured for instant navigation. If it isn't, start with the [Instant navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) to validate its caching structure first.
40 	
41 	## Resolve URL data at prefetch time
42 	
43 	Set `<Link prefetch={true}>` to resolve URL data for that link before navigation. The destination must use [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/partialPrefetching), enabled globally with `partialPrefetching` or per segment with [`prefetch = 'partial'`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch#partial).
44 	
45 	A user on `/` sees links to `/search?q=react` and `/search?q=next`, each opting in with `prefetch={true}`:
46 	
47 	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
48 	import Link from 'next/link'
49 	
50 	export default function Home() {
51 	  return (
52 	    <nav>
53 	      <Link href="/search?q=react" prefetch={true}>
54 	        React
55 	      </Link>
56 	      <Link href="/search?q=next" prefetch={true}>
57 	        Next.js
58 	      </Link>
59 	    </nav>
60 	  )
61 	}
62 	```
63 	
64 	`'auto'` is equivalent to omitting `prefetch` or passing `undefined`. In a conditional expression, return `'auto'` for links that should keep the default App Shell prefetch:
65 	
66 	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx"
67 	<Link href={href} prefetch={isFeatured ? true : 'auto'} />
68

2  	title: Ensuring instant navigations
3  	description: Learn how to structure your app to prefetch and prerender more content, providing instant page loads and client navigations.
4  	nav_title: Instant navigation
5  	related:
6  	  title: Learn more
7  	  description: Explore the full instant API, caching, and revalidation.
8  	  links:
9  	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant
10 	    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
11 	    - app/getting-started/caching
12 	    - app/getting-started/revalidating
13 	    - app/guides/prefetching
14 	---
15 	
16 	This guide walks through understanding instant navigations, writing a route that navigates instantly, visualizing what's in the initial UI, and locking the behavior in with end-to-end tests.
17 	
18 	## What "instant" means
19 	
20 	A navigation is **instant** when the browser can start rendering the new page the moment the user clicks, with static, cached, and fallback content showing up right away, while the server streams the remaining content into its fallbacks.
21 	
22 	> **Good to know:** This definition assumes caches are warm. Cold caches still require the server to compute the cached result once, so the first navigation to a route may still wait.
23 	
24 	A direct visit and a client navigation to the same route can produce different initial UI. **Direct visits** get the [**static shell**](/docs/app/glossary#static-shell) as HTML, typically from a CDN. **Client navigations** only re-render below the layout the current and destination routes share, so the fallback UI defined by a `<Suspense>` boundary above that point can't be used during the transition.
25 	
26 	Whether the new page appears instantly depends on the `<Suspense>` boundaries and caching present below the shared layout.
27 	
28 	<details>
29 	<summary>Why page loads and client navigations produce different initial UI</summary>
30 	
31 	On a page load, the entire page renders from the document root. Every component runs on the server, and anything that suspends is caught by the nearest `<Suspense>` boundary in the full tree.
32 	
33 	On a client navigation between `/store/shoes` and `/store/hats`, only the components below the `/store` layout re-render. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout covers everything on a page load, but on this navigation, it sits above the re-render scope and does not trigger.
34 	
35 	This is also why client-side hooks behave differently. `useSearchParams()` suspends during server rendering because search params are not available at build time. But on a client navigation, the router already has the params from the URL and the hook resolves synchronously. The same component can render immediately on a client navigation but sit behind a fallback on a page load.
36 	
37 	</details>
38 	
39 	With `prefetch={true}`, per-link prefetching resolves a link's URL data (`searchParams` and `params`) before navigation. First make the route instant with its App Shell. Per-link prefetching cannot fix a route that blocks without it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) for the patterns.
40 	
41 	## Quick start
42 	
43 	Getting the most out of Instant Navigation requires enabling [Cache Components](/docs/app/guides/migrating-to-cache-components) and [Partial Prefetching](/docs/app/guides/adopting-partial-prefetching), then following the [validation errors](#validate-instant-navigation) that appear:
44 	
45 	```ts filename="next.config.ts"
46 	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
47 	
48 	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
49 	  cacheComponents: true,
50 	  partialPrefetching: true,
51 	}
52 	
53 	export default nextConfig
54 	```
55 	
56 	To help you automate this process with an agent, there's a Skill for each part, [next-cache-components-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-cache-components-adoption) and [next-partial-prefetching-adoption](https://www.skills.sh/vercel/next.js/next-partial-prefetching-adoption).

node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/03-file-conventions/02-route-segment-config/instant.md 1 --- 2 title: instant 3 description: API reference for the instant route segment config. 4 related: 5 title: Next Steps 6 description: Learn how to use instant navigations in practice. 7 links: 8 - app/guides/instant-navigation 9 - app/getting-started/caching 10 - app/getting-started/revalidating 11 - app/api-reference/directives/use-cache 12 --- 13 14 The `instant` route segment config controls how Next.js validates whether a navigation into this segment would produce an instant UI. 15 16 Next.js uses prefetching to preload navigations for all in-app links on the current page. However, client-side data fetching or partially prerendered results from the server can lead to navigations that don't update the UI immediately. To help you build fast-feeling navigations, `instant` lets you tell Next.js what to expect from navigations through the configured segment. For instance, you can indicate that navigations into this segment should produce a UI that renders instantly without waiting on any externally loaded data. You can also indicate that navigations aren't expected to be instant. 17 18 When a segment is configured to expect an instant UI, Next.js surfaces any code in your application that would block the navigation from updating the UI immediately. See the [Instant Navigation guide](/docs/app/guides/instant-navigation) for an end-to-end walkthrough. 19 20 > **Good to know**: 21 > 22 > - The `instant` export only works when [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) is enabled. 23 > - `instant` cannot be used in Client Components. ...
31 } 32 ``` 33 34 ```jsx filename="layout.js | page.js" switcher 35 export const instant = true 36 37 export default function Page() { 38 return
...
39 } 40 ``` 41 42 ## Reference 43 44 The export accepts: 45 46 - **`true`**: Opts the segment into validation at whatever level is configured globally (see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults)). With the framework defaults, validation runs in development only and surfaces errors in the dev overlay. 47 - **`false`**: Opts the segment out (see [Disabling instant](#disabling-instant)). 48 - An **object**: Opts in with additional options. See [`level`](#level). 49 50 ### `level` 51 52 Sets the severity at which validation runs for this segment. 53 54 ```tsx filename="page.tsx" 55 export const instant = { 56 level: 'warning', 57 } 58 ``` 59 60 - **`'warning'`**: Validates in development only. Errors appear in the dev overlay; the build is unaffected. 61 62 In the future a validation level that supports validation during build will be supported. Unless you are enabling experimental validation modes there is no need to specify level since the only level available is `"warning"`. 63 64 When `level` is omitted (or `instant = true` is used), the segment is validated at whatever level is configured globally — see [Configuring validation defaults](#configuring-validation-defaults). 65 66 ### Disabling instant 67 68 Set `false` on a layout or page to indicate that this segment is allowed to block when navigating to it. 69 70 This is useful when a deeper page should be instant but an ancestor can't be. For instance, if a shared layout cannot load instantly but you still want to assert that pages beneath this layout can be navigated to instantly, you can ensure that the pages have `instant = true` while the shared layout has `instant = false`. 71

73 	The rest of this guide covers the tools these migrations use, walks a navigation that blocks to instant, inspects what lands in the initial UI, and locks the result in with end-to-end tests.
74 	
75 	## The tools
76 	
77 	### Build the static shell
78 	
79 	With Cache Components, **caching directives** (`"use cache"` and its variants) assign a lifetime to an async function's result, which is what lets Next.js include it in the static shell.
80 	
81 	> **Good to know:** [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache-private) is a variant for caching functions that read runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`. The result is cached in the browser only, not on the server. **It can't be part of the static shell.** See [`"use cache: private"`](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching#use-cache-private) in the Optimizing prefetching guide for how it pairs with prefetching.
82 	
83 	**`<Suspense>`** declares fallback UI for parts of the tree that read uncached data or runtime APIs like `cookies()` and `headers()`; the content streams into the fallback when it resolves.
84 	
85 	> **Good to know:** A fallback may access `cookies()`, `headers()`, or the full URL. At build time, the fallback itself suspends, and a `<Suspense>` boundary further up the tree is needed. For a link with `prefetch={true}`, [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) makes URL data available before navigation, so the fallback can become part of the prefetched UI. Cached values like timestamps or data fetches can sit directly inside the fallback.
86 	
87 	Next.js can also generate an [**App Shell**](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route, which renders during client navigations while remaining content streams. 88 	
89 	### Prefetch URL data for a link
90

92 	
93 	To prefetch the page content alongside the shell for a specific link, set [`prefetch={true}`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch):
94 	
95 	```tsx
96 	<Link href="/checkout" prefetch>
97 	  Checkout
98 	</Link>
99 	```
100	
101	With Partial Prefetching enabled, `prefetch={true}` also opts the link into [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching), which resolves the per-link URL data (`params`, `searchParams`, the full URL) ahead of the click.
102	
103	### Validate instant navigation
104	
105	By **default** (`validationLevel: 'warning'`), Cache Components apps validate every Page and Default segment in development. Validation surfaces what would keep navigations into a segment from being instant — which navigations would block, where a `<Suspense>` boundary is missing, and which data is reaching the user uncached.
106	
107	To opt out of automatic validation and only validate segments that explicitly export `instant`, set [`validationLevel`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/instant#configuring-validation-defaults) to `'manual-warning'`:
108	
109	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={7}
110	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
111	
112	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
113	  cacheComponents: true,
114	  experimental: {
115	    instantInsights: {
116	      validationLevel: 'manual-warning',
117	    },
118	  },
119	}
120	
121	export default nextConfig
122	```
123	
124	<details>
125	<summary>How validation simulates different navigations</summary>
126	
127	For each validated route, Next.js checks both the initial page load and client navigations at different points in the route hierarchy.
128	
129	For a route like `/shop/[slug]`, validation checks:
130	
131	- **Page load**: the full tree renders from the root. The root layout `<Suspense>` catches everything.
132	- **Client navigation** (e.g. from `/shop/shoes` to `/shop/hats`): the `/shop` layout is already mounted and only the page below it re-renders. A `<Suspense>` boundary in the root layout does not cover this navigation.
133	
134	Each case is validated independently. A `<Suspense>` boundary that covers one navigation path might not cover another. This is why a page can pass the page load check but fail for client navigations, and why catching these issues by hand is difficult as the number of routes grows.
135	
136	</details>

See [Prevent regressions with e2e tests](#prevent-regressions-with-e2e-tests) for the pattern.

142	### Inspect loading states
143

145	
146	Pair it with the React DevTools Suspense panel to see exactly which boundary covers which part of the page. See [Visualize loading states with the Next.js DevTools](#visualize-loading-states-with-the-nextjs-devtools) for the workflow.

148	See [Maximizing the static shell](/docs/app/getting-started/caching#maximizing-the-static-shell) for patterns to reduce fallback coverage and pull more content into the shell.

<path>node_modules/next/dist/docs/01-app/03-api-reference/05-config/01-next-config-js/partialPrefetching.md</path>
<content>
1 	---
2 	title: partialPrefetching
3 	description: Configure the default link prefetch behavior to fetch only the static parts of each route.
4 	related:
5 	  title: Related
6 	  description: View related API references and guides.
7 	  links:
8 	    - app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents
9 	    - app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch
10	    - app/api-reference/components/link
11	    - app/guides/optimizing-prefetching
12	---
13	
14	`partialPrefetching` enables Partial Prefetching at the app level. The framework prefetches the static parts of each route by default; set `prefetch={true}` on individual links to use [per-link prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching) and fetch more.
15	
16	## Usage
17	
18	```ts filename="next.config.ts" highlight={5} switcher
19	import type { NextConfig } from 'next'
20	
21	const nextConfig: NextConfig = {
22	  cacheComponents: true,
23	  partialPrefetching: true,
24	}
25	
26	export default nextConfig
27	```
28	
29	```js filename="next.config.js" highlight={3} switcher
30	module.exports = {
31	  cacheComponents: true,
32	  partialPrefetching: true,
33	}
34	```
35	
36	`partialPrefetching` requires [`cacheComponents`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents). Without it, `next dev` and `next build` throw at config validation.
37	
38	## Reference
39	
40	| Value   | Description                                 |
41	| ------- | ------------------------------------------- |
42	| `true`  | Enables Partial Prefetching across the app. |
43	| `false` | Default. No change to prefetch behavior.    |
44	
45	## How prefetches resolve
46	
47	Before Partial Prefetching, Next.js prefetched per visible link: a page with N links to N routes produced ~N route prefetches as those links entered the viewport.
48	
49	With `partialPrefetching: true`, Next.js prefetches one reusable [App Shell](/docs/app/glossary#app-shell) per route instead. The App Shell contains rendered output that does not depend on a link's URL. URL-specific content, including content that depends on `params` or `searchParams`, resolves after navigation by default. App Shells are cached on the client, so links to the same route reuse one prefetch.
50	
51	The pattern is similar to per-route code splitting in single-page apps: one artifact per route, shared by every link that points to it.
52	
53	> **Good to know**: Routes that read `cookies()` or `headers()` produce an App Shell that includes session data. The framework auto-detects this and caches the shell per session on the client.
54	
55	A link can ask for more than the App Shell with [`<Link prefetch={true}>`](/docs/app/api-reference/components/link#prefetch). The prefetch also resolves URL data like `params`, `searchParams`, and the full URL, and the cached content behind it. See [Optimizing prefetching](/docs/app/guides/optimizing-prefetching).
56	
57	> **Good to know**: If you use `<Link prefetch={true}>` to a route that hasn't opted into Partial Prefetching, a dev console error suggests enabling `partialPrefetching` app-wide or `prefetch = 'partial'` on the segment. The [dev warning Insight](/docs/messages/instant-link-prefetch-partial) covers each fix in detail.
58	
59	## Per-segment overrides
60	
61	A segment that exports an explicit [`prefetch`](/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/route-segment-config/prefetch) value overrides the app-level default for that route.
62	
63	## Version History
64	
65	| Version | Change                                                                     |
66	| ------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
67	| 16.3.0  | `partialPrefetching` introduced. Requires `cacheComponents` to be enabled. |
</content>

It should be used alongside the [`use cache`](/docs/app/api-reference/directives/use-cache) directive, and within the scope of the function or component. 15 16 ## Usage 17 18 ### Basic setup 19 20 To use `cacheLife`, first enable the [`cacheComponents` flag](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/cacheComponents) in your `next.config.js` file: 21 22 ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher 23 import type { NextConfig } from 'next' 24 25 const nextConfig: NextConfig = { 26 cacheComponents: true, 27 } 28 29 export default nextConfig 30 ``` 31 32 ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher 33 const nextConfig = { 34 cacheComponents: true, 35 } 36 37 module.exports = nextConfig 38 ``` 39 40 `cacheLife` can only be used within a cache directive scope. 41 42 Add a cache directive (for example, `use cache`) at the file level or at the top of an async function or component. 43 44 `cacheLife` cannot be used at module scope. Calling it at the top level of a file will throw an error. 45 46 > **Good to know**: 47 > 48 > - We recommend setting a `cacheLife` in every `use cache` scope so its behavior is clear at the call site. Omitting it leaves the lifetime implicit (the `default` profile applies), which makes it harder to reason about, for example in [nested cached scopes](#nested-caching-behavior). 49 > - Call `cacheLife` in the same function or component where caching is defined. Avoid abstracting it into shared utilities so the cache behavior remains explicit and easy to reason about. 50 > - If you call `cacheLife`, ensure only one call executes per function invocation. You can call it in different control flow branches, but only one should run per request. See the [conditional cache lifetimes](#conditional-cache-lifetimes) example. 51 52 ### Using preset profiles 53 54 Next.js provides preset cache profiles that cover common caching needs. Each profile balances three factors: 55 56 - How long users see cached content without checking for updates (client-side) 57 - How often fresh content is generated on the server 58 - When old content expires completely 59 60 Choose a profile based on how frequently your content changes: 61 62 - **`seconds`** - Real-time data (stock prices, live scores) 63 - **`minutes`** - Frequently updated (social feeds, news) 64 - **`hours`** - Multiple daily updates (product inventory, weather) 65 - **`days`** - Daily updates (blog posts, articles) 66 - **`weeks`** - Weekly updates (podcasts, newsletters) 67 - **`max`** - Rarely changes (legal pages, archived content) 68 69 Import `cacheLife` and pass a profile name: 70 71 ```tsx filename="app/blog/page.tsx" highlight={1,5} 72 'use cache' 73 import { cacheLife } from 'next/cache' 74 75 export default async function BlogPage() { 76 cacheLife('days') // Blog content updated daily 77 78 const posts = await getBlogPosts() 79 return
{/* render posts */}
80 } 81 ``` 82 83 The profile name tells Next.js how to cache the entire function's output. If you don't call `cacheLife`, the `default` profile is used. See [preset cache profiles](#preset-cache-profiles) for timing details. 84 85 ## Reference 86 87 ### Cache profile properties 88 89 Cache profiles control caching behavior through three timing properties: 90 91 - **[`stale`](#stale)**: How long the client can use cached data with

1 	---
2 	title: Link Component
3 	description: Enable fast client-side navigation with the built-in `next/link` component.
4 	---
5 	
6 	{/* The content of this doc is shared between the app and pages router. You can use the `<PagesOnly>Content</PagesOnly>` component to add content that is specific to the Pages Router. Any shared content should not be wrapped in a component. */}
7 	
8 	`<Link>` is a React component that extends the HTML `<a>` element to provide [prefetching](/docs/app/getting-started/linking-and-navigating#prefetching) and client-side navigation between routes. It is the primary way to navigate between routes in Next.js.
9 	
10	Basic usage:
11	
12	<AppOnly>
13	
14	```tsx filename="app/page.tsx" switcher
15	import Link from 'next/link'
16	
17	export default function Page() {
18	  return <Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
19	}
20	```
21	
22	```jsx filename="app/page.js" switcher
23	import Link from 'next/link'
24	
25	export default function Page() {
26	  return <Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
27	}
28	```
29	
30	</AppOnly>
31	
32	<PagesOnly>
33	
34	```tsx filename="pages/index.tsx" switcher
35	import Link from 'next/link'
36	
37	export default function Home() {
38	  return <Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
39	}
40	```
41	
42	```jsx filename="pages/index.js" switcher
43	import Link from 'next/link'
44	
45	export default function Home() {
46	  return <Link href="/dashboard">Dashboard</Link>
47	}
48	```
49	
50	</PagesOnly>
51	
52	## Reference
53	
54	The following props can be passed to the `<Link>` component:
55	
56	<PagesOnly>
57	
58	| Prop                        | Example                  | Type              | Required |
59	| --------------------------- | ------------------------ | ----------------- | -------- |
60	| [`href`](#href-required)    | `href="/dashboard"`      | String or Object  | Yes      |
61	| [`as`](#as)                 | `as="/post/abc"`         | String or Object  | -        |
62	| [`replace`](#replace)       | `replace={false}`        | Boolean           | -        |
63	| [`scroll`](#scroll)         | `scroll={false}`         | Boolean           | -        |
64	| [`prefetch`](#prefetch)     | `prefetch={false}`       | Boolean           | -        |
65	| [`shallow`](#shallow)       | `shallow={false}`        | Boolean           | -        |
66	| [`locale`](#locale)         | `locale="fr"`            | String or Boolean | -        |
67	| [`onNavigate`](#onnavigate) | `onNavigate={(e) => {}}` | Function          | -        |
68	
69	</PagesOnly>
70	
71	<AppOnly>
72	
73	| Prop                                  | Example                          | Type                       | Required |
74	| ------------------------------------- | -------------------------------- | -------------------------- | -------- |
75	| [`href`](#href-required)              | `href="/dashboard"`              | String or Object           | Yes      |

events.content:
Navigating from the dashboard to a project now shows that project's title immediately, without prefetching the rest of the page.

- Dashboard links use `prefetch={true}`, so the cached title is ready before the click.
- The title and the rest of the page are separate. The description and activity wait on `navigation()`, so they stay out of the prefetch and stream in after navigation.
- Partial prefetching is on, which is what lets that per-link prefetch include the title without the rest of the page.

`npm run build` completed successfully (exit 0). A production prefetch for `/projects/acme` included "Acme Storefront" and omitted the description and activity. A full navigation included both.
